newsitem.title: FRANCE: FRANCE SEEN ESTIMATING 14.9 MLN TONNE MAIZE CROP.
newsitem.headline: FRANCE SEEN ESTIMATING 14.9 MLN TONNE MAIZE CROP.

text.p: The French farm ministry is preparing to issue a 1997 maize production forecast of around 14.9 million tonnes, the second largest crop on record, French grain sources said on Monday.
The forecast, the ministry's first for French maize to be harvested in 1997, is expected to be released from Tuesday.
It compares with a 1996 crop last estimated by the ministry at 14.4 million tonnes and a 1993 record of 15 million tonnes.
The ministry has already published an estimate of a 2.7 percent increase in maize sowings to 1.73 million hectares, though the semi-public cereals office ONIC puts the area increase near one percent.
Crop analysts say maize is growing in generally favourable conditions despite some lingering concerns over moisture.
In other categories, the French farm ministry was expected to hold its soft wheat production forecast broadly steady at 33.2 million tonnes, down from a record 34.6 million last year.
Sources said it may also project a barley harvest close to 10 million tonnes, compared with a July estimate of 9.7 million and 1996 output of 9.5 million.

It would cut its forecast for durum production to some 937,000 tonnes from 974,000 published last month. The grain was hit by drought in the first quarter of 1997 and output has dropped by a quarter since last year.
The ministry was expected to echo industry forecasts of a record rapeseed crop above three million tonnes this year.
Sources said it would lift its estimate for 1997 rapeseed output to some 3.15 million tonnes from 2.84 million tonnes and last year's production of 2.91 million.
Earlier on Monday the French oilseeds association SIDO said it was targeting a crop above three million tonnes.
